AREA FORECAST DISCUSSION
National Weather Service Wakefield VA
616 AM EDT Sat Aug 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

  Marginal (level 1/5) risk for eastern VA and the MD Eastern 
  Shore

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 305 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Showers and some embedded storms are likely today, 
especially near the Chesapeake Bay and on the Eastern Shore. While 
severe weather is not expected, localized flash flooding will be 
possible. 

A weak stationary boundary remains just south of the forecast area 
this morning, roughly aligned along the NC/SC coast. There is also a 
broad trough axis aloft across most of the eastern CONUS. Locally, 
there is a ribbon of mostly light rain across the 
northern/northwest portions of the area. This conflicts with several 
earlier runs of various CAMS which depicted rather widespread 
overnight showers and storms, particularly across SE VA and NE NC. 
In fact, these areas are actually quite stable as of this writing 
with sfc temps in the lower 70s and dew points in the upper 60s, 
which yields low/near-zero sfc-based and MUCAPE. Any 
appreciable instability remains confined to our S, in closer 
proximity to the front. Therefore, really don't see much 
convective activity developing through around sunrise. 

The front will (eventually) lift northward as we head into this 
afternoon. Model and WPC progs also depict weak low pressure 
developing in the vicinity of the Chesapeake Bay and Eastern Shore. 
This, combined with some low-level convergence, should be sufficient 
for showers to develop in these areas by late this afternoon and 
afternoon. Instability looks quite meager, especially early on in 
the day, so am not expecting widespread thunderstorms at this time. 
A moist atmospheric column (PWATS ~2.1" across the E/SE) and slow-
moving activity will support a continued heavy rain and localized 
flash flooding risk. The 00z HREF also depicted a relatively 
impressive signal for heavy rain and some flash flooding in the 
Eastern Shore vicinity. However, all of the 00z members that 
comprised the ensemble suite are currently handling the ongoing 
activity extremely poorly. Therefore, confidence in the evolution of 
convection later today is low and some recent runs of the CAMs are 
less bullish about the overall coverage of showers and the
associated heavy rain signal. WPC has removed the targeted 
"Slight" excessive rainfall risk (which was in place for eastern
VA and the MD Eastern Shore) and replaced it with a broad 
"Marginal" risk. In summary, localized pockets of very heavy 
rain are possible, but the exact location is uncertain and the  
coverage may tend to be on the low side. All of this precludes 
the need for any Flood Watch at this time. Late this evening, 
convection from the Great Lakes and OH Valley, associated with 
the primary cold front and trough, could approach our Piedmont 
counties. However, diminishing instability and reduced forcing
with eastward extent should allow for most of this activity to 
diminish as it moves eastward tonight. 

Outside of any precip, temps will be quite "cool" for mid-late 
August and only in the upper 70s-lower 80s (some mid 80s possible 
SE). Skies will average mostly cloudy, with some clearing possible W 
of I-95 this afternoon.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Mainly dry with seasonable temperatures Sunday 
through Tuesday. Isolated to scattered diurnally driven convection 
returns by the middle to latter part of the week.

The weak front will finally move offshore late Sunday, as the main 
upper level trough axis shifts offshore and surface high pressure 
builds into the SE CONUS. The surface high will usher in a drier 
airmass with seasonable temperatures in the 80s and dew points in 
the 60s Sunday into early next week. A reinforcing intrusion of dry 
air is likely Monday night/Tuesday with dew points in the 50s 
looking likely (except 60s far SE). The high is progged to break
down by Wed/Thu, with unsettled conditions and isolated- 
scattered aftn/evening convection returning mid to late week.

&&

.AVIATION /10Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
As of 615 AM EDT Saturday...

A frontal boundary remains just south of the area as of 10z,
with most sites (stubbornly) remaining VFR. Still expect a
period of lower CIGs at the terminals for a time this morning,
especially at/near RIC and there could be very localized IFR
CIGs. Additionally, the coverage of showers/storms is expected 
to increase over the next few hours and especially after 12z. 
While strong-severe storms are not expected today, IFR VSBYs are
possible in any heavier showers. Remaining unsettled heading 
into the later half of the day with continued showers/storms 
expected (best chance SBY/PHF/ORF/ECG). CIGs should remain MVFR 
through most of the morning and should gradually lift to VFR by
this afternoon and especially this evening. SBY potentially
stays sub-VFR most of the day. Drying out tonight with VFR
conditions returning, though can't rule out some patchy fog
inland. 

Outlook: Drying out tonight with VFR conditions returning 
Sunday morning through Monday. Some patchy fog could occur
inland around or after 06z Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 305 AM EDT Saturday...

Key Messages:

- Generally benign marine conditions are expected through the 
  weekend into early next week.

- Showers and occasional thunderstorms are expected today, with
  diminishing chances of showers and thunderstorms Sunday into 
  early next week.

Sub-SCA conditions are expected to prevail this weekend through much 
of next week. Weak high pressure is centered over Atlantic Canada 
early this morning, with a weak trough off the NC Outer Banks. The 
wind is E 5-10kt. Seas are 2-3ft, with ~1ft waves in the Ches. Bay. 
A weak trough lingers offshore today as a warm front lifts across 
the Mid-Atlantic coast. An E wind is forecast to increase to 10-15kt 
across the northern coastal/offshore waters this morning, before 
becoming SE ~10kt this aftn. Elsewhere, generally an E/SE wind ~10kt 
for the Ches. Bay, SE/S 5-10kt for the southern coastal/offshore 
waters, tidal rivers, and Currituck Sound. Numerous showers/tstms 
are expected today as the warm front lifts across the waters. The 
wind becomes SW 5-10kt tonight ahead of a weak cold front, which 
cross the coast early Sunday resulting in a wind shift to W 5-10kt. 
Another weak cold front crosses the coast early Monday with a brief 
wind shift to NW, before becoming W/SW with speeds remaining less 
than 10kt. Yet another weak cold front crosses the coast early 
Tuesday resulting in a brief wind shift to NNW. High pressure 
settles off the Southeast coast mid to late next week resulting in 
S/SW flow at or below 15kt. Seas are expected to be 2ft to 
occasionally 3ft for the next week, with 1ft to occasionally 2ft 
waves in the Ches. Bay.

A low rip risk will be maintained today, Sunday, and Monday. There 
is a period of increased onshore flow for the northern beaches this 
morning. However, the swell direction will be ~50 degrees for shore 
normal, which should result in more of a longshore current. This 
combined with shorter period nearshore waves should keep the rip 
risk at low for the northern beaches today.
